Marc Pingris and Paul Artadi didn't only lose a former teammate when Peter June ‘PJ’ Simon passed away last Friday. They also lost a friend.

Beyond the battles they shared on the PBA court, Simon forged a bond with his teammates that went far beyond basketball.

And Pingris and Artadi made sure Simon's legacy would be remembered as they recalled moments with him.
Pingris, who formed the Purefoods' 'Big Three' alongside Simon and James Yap, said their chemistry on the court was unmatched, which helped them steer the franchise to a rare Grand Slam as they won the 2014 Philippine Cup, 2014 Commissioner’s Cup, and 2014 Governors’ Cup.
"Maganda ‘yung chemistry namin, especially sa aming tatlo nila James," Pingris said in an interview with Kapuso Mo Jessica Sojo.
"Parang sabi namin, ‘tol, hindi natin akalain na magagawa natin ‘to kasi ang hirap manalo ng isang championship e’."
(We had good chemisty, especially the three of us with James… We said, ‘tol, we never thought we would be able to do this because it’s so hard to win a championship.)
Artadi was also emotional remembering Simon, sharing their memories they forged in life after their professional career.
"Very, very generous ‘yan. Nu’ng nag-retire na kami as a PBA player, nagsama kami sa PBA Motoclub. Ang trabaho ng PBA Motoclub ay umikot sa buong mundo para pasiyahin ‘yung mga OFWs natin," Artadi added.
(He’s very, very generous. When we were already retired as PBA players, we came together at PBA Motoclub. The job of PBA Motoclub was to go around the world, bringing happiness to our OFWs.)
Artadi also recalled the times he and Simon both entered the league as rookies and said the latter never took it personal whenever he only got limited time on court.
"2004, sabay kaming nag-PBA. Syempre rookie days mo at hindi mo alam kung tatagal ka sa PBA eh kasi ang daming magagaling eh. Pero in spite of that, kahit anong nangyari sa kanya, kahit hindi siya gamitin, kahit bangko siya, continued pa rin ‘yung hard work niya," Artadi said.
"Talagang mabigat si PJ Simon, dalawa ‘yung moniker niya,” he added, referring to Simon’s nicknames of the ‘Scoring Apostle’ and ‘Super Sub’.
(2004, we came into the PBA at the same time. Of course, in your rookie days, you don’t know if you’ll last a long time in the PBA because there are so many good players. But in spite of that, whatever happened with him, even if he didn’t play, even if he was on the bench, he always continued with his hard work… PJ Simon really was so good, he had two monikers.)
—Bea Micaller/JMB, GMA News
